- When sentiment is positive (≥0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.10), model frequently overcorrects downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to avoid mean reversion trap.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.50 or 0.25 in consecutive days), model often fails to anticipate downward correction; add 1–2% downward bias in next 5–7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model is consistently >85% of true outcome, apply “lag correction”: subtract 1–3% for each day beyond 10-day horizon where sentiment is flat or negative.
